Today's verdict BEARISH-DEFENSIVE
When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index 1/10 — price action calm, only 1-2 signals active vs VIX Spike Tier 4/4 EXTREME — 85% probability, backwardation and skew both active
Options market is pricing a move before it appears in spot price distribution. Trust the VIX tier first: options flow leads spot price, and three sub-signals firing simultaneously (skew, backwardation, adaptive) is institutional hedging against a specific near-term tail, not background noise.
Today's tension
Options market at maximum alert while price action registers near-zero distribution stress
Bull
The Crash Index at **1/10** confirms only **1-2** signals active and the regime scores STABLE at **28**. Korea's **+6.9%** five-day gain shows real risk appetite exists in at least one corner of the global market.
Bear
VIX Spike hits Tier **4/4** EXTREME at **85%** probability with backwardation, skew, and adaptive signal all firing together. The options market is priced for a vol expansion that hasn't shown up in spot yet, and options positioning typically leads price.
The tell: Watch VIX term structure. Backwardation resolving signals the options fear premium deflating. Backwardation deepening alongside any one of the three inactive confluence pairs (HYG, small-cap drawdown, or yen) activating would signal the Crash Index is about to catch up.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The central tension today is a clean split between price and options markets. The Crash Index at 1/10 says spot markets are quiet, with only 1-2 distribution signals active. The VIX Spike Detector disagrees at Tier 4/4 EXTREME, 85% probability, with skew, backwardation, and the adaptive signal all live simultaneously. The regime scores 28 (STABLE) with a MIXED bias, which is exactly what you get when two signal sets are reading the same market differently. The macro regime leans INFLATIONARY at only 45% confidence, barely above a coin flip.

For positioning, the VIX extreme is the dominant read. Skew active means the options market is paying a premium specifically for downside. Backwardation means near-term vol is elevated above longer-dated vol, a structure that typically marks fear of a specific near-term event rather than diffuse background concern. Three VIX sub-components firing at once is institutional hedging. The Contrarian score at 31 sits neutral, so there is no crowded position to fade in either direction. You carry protective positioning at higher-than-normal weight while the price tape is still quiet.

The main risk is being early on the vol premium. If VIX term structure normalizes and backwardation resolves, the options market's fear was premature and the STABLE regime reading wins. The specific data point that would flip the stance: a VIX backwardation confluence with HYG credit stress, small-cap drawdown, or yen safe-haven flow activating. Currently all three confluence pairs are inactive, and that absence is the only thing keeping this from a full risk-off read.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The macro regime reads INFLATIONARY but only at 45% confidence. The regime state scores 28 (STABLE) with a MIXED bias.

At 45% confidence you can't lean hard into either the inflation playbook (long commodities, short duration) or the disinflation playbook (long duration, growth), because the system sees competing forces of roughly equal weight. The XLE vs XLK correlation breakdown and the TLT vs SHY yield-curve drift (from -0.03 to -0.65) are the live market inputs into this regime question.

Until confidence moves decisively above its current 45%, the INFLATIONARY call is contested, and position sizing around it should stay proportionate to the limited conviction behind it.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

The divergence composite labels the zone as CALM, but 44% of tracked pairs are diverging, the net tilt runs 17 bearish pairs against 2 bullish, and the Mother Jaws composite scores a maximum 100. Divergence here means pairs of assets that historically move in a consistent relationship have broken that relationship.

Correlation drift measures how far that relationship has shifted from its baseline. The XLE vs XLK pair drifted from -0.55 to +0.16: energy and tech, which normally move inversely, are now moving together, a sign that macro forces are overriding sector fundamentals.

TLT vs SHY moved from -0.03 to -0.65: long-duration bonds are breaking away from short-duration in a quiet yield-curve regime shift. USMV vs SPY flipped from -0.86 to +0.22, meaning the low-volatility defensive factor now moves with the broad index rather than against it, a sign that its offsetting quality has broken down.

AUD/JPY vs SPY deepened to -0.90: risk FX and US equities are moving in sharply opposite directions, a classic early read on background risk-off pressure. The 17-to-2 bearish tilt in correlation drift is the signal the CALM composite label does not capture.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Korea is the only positive performer across the five-day global snapshot at +6.9%, while Australia lags Asia at -2.2%. Europe is uniformly negative: STOXX50E at -1.8% is the region's relative outperformer, the Swiss Market Index at -4.5% the laggard.

In the US, Nasdaq holds at -0.4% while the Russell 2000 drops -2.2%, a 1.8 percentage point spread that rewards large-cap tech and penalizes small-cap cyclicals. Crypto follows the same pattern: ETH at -0.1% outperforms BTC at -3.9%.

The read across all four regions is consistent: anything economically sensitive or higher-beta is underperforming, while large-cap tech holds its ground as the relative anchor. The US session opens into a backdrop where global pressure is broad, most indices are down 2% or more over five days, and Korea's +6.9% is the single outlier in an otherwise uniform global decline.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 1/10 and the VIX Spike Detector at Tier 4/4 EXTREME are reading different layers of the same market, and both can be simultaneously correct. The Crash Index counts distribution signals in price: with only 1-2 active, spot markets haven't begun the kind of selling that registers as crash risk.

The VIX tier measures options market pricing directly. At 85% probability with skew active, backwardation active, and the adaptive trigger live, institutional desks are paying for downside protection against a move that hasn't yet appeared in price.

This gap is a standard pre-event structure. Options market hedging leads price deterioration, sometimes by days.

The Crash Index will catch up if the vol expansion the options market is pricing actually arrives.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). STRESS = liquidity tension (HYG, MOVE, STLFSI). TOPPING = end-of-cycle signals (concentration, breadth narrowing, defensives leading). Doctrine: a single signal = noise. 3+ aligned in one bucket = real confirmed regime.

How to read
Heat ranking: composite of RS (relative strength vs SPY), Momentum (price action 20-60d), Breadth (% stocks above SMA), Options flow, and Attention. Use top-5 as rotation focus.
Emerging industries: high velocity = screener scores accelerating this week vs prior baseline — potential early rotation signal.
Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
